HPE Deliverables: • HPE to work with NREL to create the correct data set for the AI model. This data will be used to train the model. • HPE to develop an AI-based model using NREL’s strategy to predict cooling system ramp/ramp down time in advance of large and power-hungry jobs. • HPE and NREL to run at least two test cases for power hungry jobs in order to verify the capability of the model to effectively predict the ramp up/ramp down of the cooling system. Task 6: Incident Tracking and ML Validation Databases (NREL and HPE) To support ongoing AIOps model validation in year three, NREL will develop an incident tracking system and support HPE in development of an ML validation database. Taken together, this system will be the single source of all anomalies (events) necessary for validation tasks. These databases will be used as a basis for training and quantifying the performance of anomaly detection models. NREL Deliverables: • Build an incident tracking database for known events in data center, and devices affected. HPE Deliverables: • HPE to create a ML Validation database with annotations of anomalies. • Use the ML Validation database to quantify the performance of the anomaly detection models. • Provide access to ML Validation database to NREL though an API. 15 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. Task 7: Edge-to-Cloud Investigation (NREL and HPE) This task was started in Year 2 but given that access to the ESIF data center was severely limited due to COVID-19 regulations, the task did not advance beyond the acquisition of the required hardware – the hardware includes an HPE EL300 server, in addition to a data acquisition system. In Year 2, NREL and HPE decided to use a CDU as an edge device for the purposes of the demonstration. In Year 3, NREL and HPE will work to install the hardware and demonstrate AIOps running at the edge (access to the ESIF data center permitting). The team will also explore the requirements for a larger to be potentially undertaken under a separate effort. NREL Deliverables: • Install the EL300 and data acquisition system and connect the data acquisition system to a CDU. • Provide HPE with network access to the EL300. • NREL to provide HPE with the data necessary to support the HPE deliverables for this task. • Store results of the analytics (see HPE Deliverables), to Druid for visualization/querying. HPE Deliverables: • Develop and deploy a model for the fluid’s secondary temperature (decided in Year 2). • Install AIOps on the EL300. • Conduct analytics on the fluid’s secondary temperature metric streamed to Kafka and write the results of the analytics back to Kafka.
